    Interactions

    Define interactions, the parts of a system that change the states of elements.

    An interaction reads the states of the elements its roles bind and returns laws that change them, such as a rate, a map, a random event, or a transfer between members.

    BaseInteraction(label)

    Bases: BasePart[BaseSpace, SimpleNamespace]

    An abstract interaction, the part of a system that changes states of elements.

    An interaction binds elements through roles, such as 'source' and 'target', reads their states, and returns laws that change them. It holds no state of its own. A state on a coupling, such as the weight of an edge, lives in a group on the edges or hyperedges of a network. A subclass takes each role and parameter as an argument of its __init__, annotated with RoleSpec or ParameterSpec inside Annotated, and stores it under the same name, as a scikit-learn estimator does. It returns its laws from _get_laws, where namespace.<role> reads the states of the element a role binds and namespace.<parameter> is a symbol.

    A role states the element kinds and states it needs in its RoleSpec, and the class lists the laws it may return in law_classes, so that get_requirements and get_tags can name them before a run. A subclass whose arguments choose among its laws overrides _get_tags. A subclass that names its roles or parameters otherwise returns their names from _get_role and _get_parameter. An interaction that draws a random order of agents, breaks ties at random, or picks members at random is stochastic whatever its laws.

    Unlike BasePart, it changes the states of other parts and holds none of its own. Choose it when a new kind of interaction runs its laws in a way of its own, as NeighborInteraction runs them once per edge. Choose Interaction for laws that run once for the elements the roles bind.

    It appears in every field through its subclasses, such as infection in an epidemic, a chemical reaction, a payment between accounts, and the coupling of oscillators.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'growth'.

    		 required

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    laws_ Sequence[BasePart]

    The laws the interaction contributes for the namespace of its last run.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import BaseInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import ParameterSpec, RoleSpec
>>> class GrowthInteraction(BaseInteraction):
...     def __init__(
...         self, label, target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()], r: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0
...     ):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.target = target
...         self.r = r
...
...     def _get_laws(self, namespace):
...         return []
>>> GrowthInteraction('growth', target='rabbits', r=0.5).get_params()
{'label': 'growth', 'r': 0.5, 'target': 'rabbits'}

    def get_requirements(self) -> InteractionRequirementSpec:
    """Return what the interaction needs.

    It needs the element kinds and states of its roles, and its laws' time and space.

    Returns:
        requirements:
            The roles by name, with the states each reads for the values of this interaction, the law classes
            the class lists, and the classes of time and of space these laws run in.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import RateInteraction
        >>> interaction = RateInteraction('growth', target='rabbits', state='n', rate=lambda s: s.target.n)
        >>> interaction.get_requirements().roles['target'].states
        ('n',)
    """
    laws = self._get_law_classes()
    needs = [law.get_requirements() for law in laws]
    return InteractionRequirementSpec(
        time=self._get_accepted([need.time for need in needs]),
        space=self._get_accepted([need.space for need in needs]),
        roles={
            name: replace(spec, states=self._get_state_names(spec.states))
            for name, spec in self._get_specs().items()
            if isinstance(spec, RoleSpec)
        },
        laws=laws,
    )

    ConnectionInteraction(label, *, members, ports)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that joins ports so that their potentials agree and flows cancel.

    A port is a named connector of an element, such as a pin of a resistor, with a potential and a flow. The interaction binds the elements of one node through a role that takes any number of elements, and names the port of each. At the node the potentials of the ports are equal and their flows sum to zero. A port that no connection names has a zero flow.

    Unlike Interaction, which returns rates or maps, it returns algebraic equations, which hold at every time. Choose it when elements with ports connect into a network of components, as in Modelica.

    It appears in many fields. Kirchhoff's laws join the pins of an electric circuit, pipes meet at a junction of a hydraulic network, and shafts join in a mechanical drive train.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'node'.

    		 required
    members Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True, elements=(ANY,))]

    The paths of the elements of the node.

    		 required
    ports Sequence[str]

    The name of the port of every element, in the same order.

    		 required

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    The members and the ports are empty or differ in length.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated, ClassVar
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import ConnectionInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws import EquationLaw
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import ConnectorSpec, ParameterSpec, StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> PIN = ConnectorSpec('pin', potential='v', flow='i')
>>> class ConductanceElement(Element):
...     ports: ClassVar = {'a': PIN}
...
...     def __init__(
...         self,
...         label,
...         a_v: Annotated[float, StateSpec(algebraic=True)] = 0.0,
...         a_i: Annotated[float, StateSpec(algebraic=True)] = 0.0,
...         g: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
...         e: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
...     ):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.a_v = a_v
...         self.a_i = a_i
...         self.g = g
...         self.e = e
...
...     def _get_laws(self, s):
...         return [EquationLaw(s.a_i, s.g * (s.a_v - s.e))]
>>> system = CompositeSystem(
...     elements=[ConductanceElement('first', e=1.0), ConductanceElement('second', e=3.0)],
...     interactions=[ConnectionInteraction('node', members=['first', 'second'], ports=['a', 'a'])],
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=1.0, dt=1.0)
>>> float(trajectory.get_values('first.a_v')[-1])
2.0

    ConservationInteraction(label, *, target, state='u', flux=None, source=None, limiter='minmod', riemann='rusanov', sources=())

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that changes a field by the divergence of a flux and a source.

    It gives the conservation law du/dt + divergence(flux) = source of a state u of a field. The flux is one expression for a field of one dimension, or one per dimension. On a finite-volume field the interaction lowers to a flux law with a slope limiter and a numerical flux, and on other fields to the rate -divergence(flux), which the field discretizes by its own operators. Without a source the total of the state on a periodic field stays constant. Several conservation laws on one field form one system, whose numerical flux reads the wave speeds of all of them. A flux or a source function takes a namespace with the field as target, the time t, and the parameters a subclass declares.

    Unlike RateInteraction, which gives the rate of a state directly, it writes the rate as the divergence of a flux, so the scheme keeps the total and captures shocks. Choose it when an amount moves through space without being created or destroyed, apart from a source.

    It appears in many fields. Cars on a road follow the traffic flow model of Lighthill and Whitham, a gas follows the Euler equations, and water in a channel follows the shallow water equations.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'traffic'.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ANY,), states=(state,), domains=RATE_DOMAINS)]

    The path of the field whose state is conserved.

    		 required
    state str

    The name of the conserved state of the field.

    		 'u'
    flux Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

    A function of the namespace that returns the flux, or one flux per dimension.

    		 None
    source Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

    A function of the namespace that returns the source, or None for none.

    		 None
    limiter str | None

    The slope limiter of the reconstruction, 'minmod', 'van-leer', or None for first order.

    		 'minmod'
    riemann str | None

    The numerical flux of a finite-volume field, 'rusanov' or 'godunov', the exact solver for one state, or None for the divergence of the flux on a field of another discretization.

    		 'rusanov'
    sources Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True, elements=(ANY,))]

    The paths of other elements the flux and the source read, as the namespaces sources. A field over the position lattice of a target on a phase space is read broadcast along the class axes.

    		 ()

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    The state is not a name, a function is not callable, or the limiter or the numerical flux is unknown.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, FieldElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import ConservationInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import LatticeSpace
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> class CellElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, u: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.u = u
>>> space = LatticeSpace((50,), spacing=0.1, boundary='periodic')
>>> values = {'u': 1.0 + np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.arange(50) / 50)}
>>> volumes = 'finite-volume'
>>> field = FieldElement('wave', element=CellElement, space=space, values=values, discretization=volumes)
>>> burgers = ConservationInteraction('burgers', target='wave', state='u', flux=lambda s: s.target.u**2 / 2)
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[field], interactions=[burgers])
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=0.5, dt=0.01)
>>> round(float(trajectory.get_values('wave.u')[-1].sum()), 6)
50.0

    def __init__(
    self,
    label: str,
    *,
    target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ElementKind.ANY,), states=('state',), domains=RATE_DOMAINS)],
    state: str = 'u',
    flux: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,

    CouplingInteraction(label, *, target, source=None, read='x', write='x', function=None, reduce='sum', mode='edges', size=None, weights=None, include_self=False, lag=0.0, delay=0.0, form='rate', combine=None, neighborhood=None, layer=None, phase=None)

    Bases: NeighborInteraction

    An interaction that combines a function of each member and its neighbours.

    Every member i of a group receives a sum, a mean, a maximum, or another reduction of function over the members j it is coupled to. By default the function is the difference x_j - x_i of the state read. The result adds to the rate of the state write, or sets its next value at every step, as form says.

    The argument mode chooses the members j:

    • 'edges': the neighbours of i along the edges of its lattice or network, or within neighborhood.
    • 'group': every other member of the group, or the members of the group source.
    • 'next': the next member in order, and the first after the last, as in a ring.
    • 'hyperedges': the other members of each hyperedge around i, a link that joins more than two members of a network.

    Unlike PairInteraction, which runs its laws for every pair within a cutoff, it reduces over the members each member is coupled to, by edges, a group, or hyperedges, and it can either add to a rate or set the next value of a state. Choose it when every member responds to an aggregate of its neighbours.

    It appears in many fields. Phase oscillators, such as fireflies that flash in step or the generators of a power grid, sum the sine of their phase differences. Heat flow between the cells of a lattice and consensus in a social network sum differences of a state. Flocks of birds and schools of fish average the headings of their neighbours within a radius.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'consensus'.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str | Sequence[str], RoleSpec(elements=(ANY,), states=(write,))]

    The path of the group of the members, such as 'people'. In the mode 'group' it may also be the path of one element, a hub that reduces over every member of source, or the paths of separate elements, each coupled to the others in the list.

    		 required
    source Annotated[str | Sequence[str] | None, RoleSpec(optional=True, elements=(ANY,))]

    The path of the group whose members are the j of the mode 'group', or None for the members of the target. It may also be the path of one element or the paths of separate elements, to which every member of the target is coupled term by term.

    		 None
    read str

    The name of the state that the default function, the delay, and the lag read, such as 'theta' for a phase.

    		 'x'
    write str | Sequence[str]

    The name of the state that the coupling changes, such as 'theta'.

    		 'x'
    function NamespaceFunction | None

    The term f_ij of one other member, a function of a namespace, or None for the difference x_j - x_i of read. The namespace reads the states of i from member, those of j from other, and the member of the edge group that joins them from edge, or None. It also holds the parameters and the time t. In the mode 'hyperedges' it reads others, the other members of one hyperedge in order, and members, all its members, in place of other, and the default sums the differences of read over the other members.

    		 None
    reduce str

    How the weighted terms w_ij f_ij combine over the members j.

    • 'sum': their sum, sum_j w_ij f_ij.
    • 'mean': the sum divided by the number of members j.
    • 'max' and 'min': the largest and the smallest term.
    • 'normalized-mean': the sum divided by the sum of the weights, sum_j w_ij f_ij / sum_j w_ij.
    • 'circular-mean': the mean angle, arctan2(sum_j w_ij sin f_ij, sum_j w_ij cos f_ij), as for headings.
    		 'sum'
    mode str

    How the members j of each member i are chosen, one of the modes above.

    		 'edges'
    size int | None

    The number of members of each hyperedge in the mode 'hyperedges', such as 3 for triangles, or None for every size.

    		 None
    weights Weights

    The weight w_ij of each term, or None for a weight of 1.

    • In the mode 'edges', the name of a state of the edge group, which a subclass binds with a second role.
    • In the mode 'group', a matrix with one row per member and one column per other member, or the name of a parameter that a subclass declares with ParameterSpec(shape=('target', 'source')).
    • In any mode, a function of the namespace of the term, such as an indicator that both members agree.
    		 None
    include_self bool

    Whether the reduction also runs over j = i.

    		 False
    lag Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()]

    The phase lag added to the state read of the member, in the units of that state, such as 0.5 radians.

    		 0.0
    delay Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    How long ago the state read of the other member is read, in units of time, or 0 for the present value.

    		 0.0
    form str

    What the reduction changes.

    • 'rate': it adds to the rate of write. The sum and the mean on the edges of a lattice or network run once per edge in both directions, and every other coupling runs once per member. On a FieldElement, a rate that is a constant times the difference of the two ends becomes that constant times the Laplacian of the field times its squared spacing, and the other end is read across the boundary conditions of the field.
    • 'map': it sets the next value of write at every step of discrete time.
    		 'rate'
    combine Combination | Callable[..., object] | None

    The next value in the form 'map', a function of the namespace of the member and the reduction, or None for the reduction itself. The namespace reads the states of i from member and holds the parameters and the time.

    		 None
    neighborhood BaseNeighborhood | None

    In the mode 'edges', the neighbourhood that gives the members j, such as RadiusNeighborhood(1.0) in a continuous space, or None for the edges of the lattice or network. In the mode 'hyperedges', the neighbourhood of a continuous space whose sets of size - 1 current neighbours form the hyperedges, or None for the hyperedges of the network.

    		 None
    layer str | None

    The layer of the network whose edges the interaction runs on, such as 'work', or None for the main graph.

    		 None
    phase str | None

    The phase of the step in which the map form runs, or None for the default phase.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    A variant is unknown, the function or the combination is not callable, the weights, the source, the reduction, or the neighbourhood do not suit the mode and the form, or the phase or the written states do not suit the form, raised by prepare.

    Examples:

    Two fireflies, as in the Kuramoto model of synchrony, pull each other by the sine of their phase difference until they flash in step.

    >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import sin
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import DeclaredElement, GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import CouplingInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import DeclaredVariableSpec, StateSpec
>>> phases = {'variables': {'theta': DeclaredVariableSpec(0.0, StateSpec())}, 'theta': [0.0, 1.0]}
>>> fireflies = GroupElement('fireflies', element=DeclaredElement, size=2, values=phases)
>>> sine = lambda s: sin(s.other.theta - s.member.theta)
>>> pull = CouplingInteraction(
...     'pull', target='fireflies', read='theta', write='theta', function=sine, mode='group'
... )
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[fireflies], interactions=[pull])
>>> simulate(system, until=4, dt=2.0).get_values('fireflies.theta').round(3).tolist()
[[0.0, 1.0], [0.49, 0.51], [0.5, 0.5]]

    Three people on a line move their opinions toward those of their neighbours until they agree on the mean.

    >>> import networkx as nx
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import NetworkSpace

    CrossingInteraction(label, *, target, guard, reset=None, direction=0, terminal=False)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that resets states or ends the run when a guard crosses zero.

    The guard is a function of the states and the time whose sign change marks an event, such as the height of a falling ball. At the crossing the event sets states of the target to new values or ends the run. A guard that reads the members of a group gives each member its own event. Solvers locate the crossing within their tolerance, and the trajectory records every crossing among its events, under the label of the interaction and with the member.

    Unlike JumpInteraction, which fires at random times, it fires at the exact time a condition on the states becomes true. Choose it when a continuous run has discrete events, such as an impact, a threshold, or a stop.

    It appears in many fields. A bouncing ball reverses its velocity at the floor, a neuron fires and resets when its potential reaches a threshold, and a thermostat switches the heater at a set temperature.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'bounce'.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ANY,), states=(reset,))]

    The path of the element or group whose states the guard reads and the event sets.

    		 required
    guard Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]

    The function guard(namespace) of the expression whose crossing of zero triggers the event.

    		 required
    reset Mapping[str, Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]] | None

    A mapping from the name of a state of the target to the function f(namespace) of its new value, applied all at once, or None to keep the states.

    		 None
    direction int

    1 for crossings from negative to positive, -1 for the opposite, and 0 for both.

    		 0
    terminal bool

    Whether the crossing ends the run.

    		 False

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    The direction is not -1, 0, or 1, or the guard or a new value is not a function.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import CrossingInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws import RateLaw
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> class ClockElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.x = x
...
...     def _get_laws(self, s):
...         return [RateLaw(s.x, 1.0)]
>>> wrap = CrossingInteraction(
...     'wrap', target='clock', guard=lambda s: s.target.x - 1, reset={'x': lambda s: 0}, direction=1
... )
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[ClockElement('clock')], interactions=[wrap])
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=2.2, dt=0.5)
>>> [round(event.time, 6) for event in trajectory.events]
[1.0, 2.0]

    EulerLagrangeInteraction(label, *, target, states='x', lagrangian=None, dissipation=None, forcing=None)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that moves coordinates by the equations of a Lagrangian.

    A Lagrangian L is the kinetic minus the potential energy of a mechanical system. The interaction gives the equations of motion d/dt dL/dq' - dL/dq = Q - dR/dq' for the coordinates q, states of order 2, with the dissipation function R and the generalized forces Q. It returns one equation per coordinate, and the compiler solves them together for the accelerations, so a Lagrangian with a mass matrix, such as that of a double pendulum, needs no inversion by hand. Equations of one coordinate from several interactions add, so a spring between two pendulums is an interaction of its own whose Lagrangian holds only the coupling energy.

    A Lagrangian, dissipation, or forcing function takes a namespace with the roles, the time t, and the parameters a subclass declares. The coordinates are the states of every role that binds one element or group, target by default, and every component of a vector state is a coordinate.

    Unlike HamiltonianInteraction, which needs canonical momenta, it takes the energy in coordinates and velocities. Choose it when the energy is easier to write than the forces, as for linked bodies.

    It appears in many fields. Pendulums and linkages in mechanics, electric circuits written by their energy, and the joints of a robot arm follow the equations of a Lagrangian.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'pendulum'.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ANY,), states=(states,))]

    The path of the element or group whose states are the coordinates.

    		 required
    states str | Sequence[str]

    The name of the state of order 2 that is a coordinate, or the names of several states.

    		 'x'
    lagrangian Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

    A function of the namespace that returns the Lagrangian.

    		 None
    dissipation Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

    A function of the namespace that returns the Rayleigh dissipation function, or None for none.

    		 None
    forcing Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

    A function of the namespace that returns the generalized forces, or None for none.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    A state is not a name, or a function is not callable.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import cos
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import EulerLagrangeInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import derivative
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> class AngleElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, q: Annotated[float, StateSpec(order=2)] = 0.1, q_d1: float = 0.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.q = q
...         self.q_d1 = q_d1
>>> swing = EulerLagrangeInteraction(
...     'swing',
...     target='bob',
...     states='q',
...     lagrangian=lambda s: derivative(s.target.q, 1) ** 2 / 2 + cos(s.target.q),
... )
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[AngleElement('bob')], interactions=[swing])
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=3.2, dt=0.01)
>>> round(float(trajectory.get_values('bob.q')[-1]), 2)
-0.1

    GradientInteraction(label, *, target, states='x', potential=None, sources=(), divisor=None, variational=False, conserved=False)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that moves states down the gradient of a potential.

    Every state x that the interaction moves gets the rate -dU/dx / d on its highest time derivative, where U is the potential and d the divisor of its member. On a state of order 1 this is a gradient flow x' = -dU/dx / d, with d a friction. On a state of order 2 it is Newton's law x'' = -dU/dx / d, with d a mass or an inertia. A vector state gets the gradient of every component.

    On a field, the potential is the density f of a functional F, the integral of f over space, and may read the field, its derivatives, and its Laplacian. With variational the field moves by the functional derivative of F, as in the Allen-Cahn equation. With conserved the rate is the Laplacian of that derivative, as in the Cahn-Hilliard equation, so the total of the field stays constant. The potential function takes a namespace with the roles, the sources, the time t, and the parameters a subclass declares.

    Unlike RateInteraction, which takes the rate itself, it takes a potential and derives the rates from it. Choose it when the dynamics descend an energy or a cost, so that one scalar function gives every rate.

    It appears in many fields. Particles move in a potential well, phases separate in an alloy, a neural network descends its loss, and cells sort by their adhesion energy.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'descent'.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ANY,), states=(states, divisor))]

    The path of the element or group whose states move.

    		 required
    states str | Sequence[str]

    The name of the state that moves, or the names of several states.

    		 'x'
    potential Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

    A function of the namespace that returns the potential, or the density of the functional of a field.

    		 None
    sources Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True, elements=(ANY,))]

    The paths of the elements or groups the potential reads but does not move.

    		 ()
    divisor str | Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | Mapping[str, str | Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]] | None

    The name of the state or parameter of every moving member that divides its rate, a function of the namespace of the member that returns the divisor, a mapping from the name of every moving state to its own divisor, or None.

    		 None
    variational bool

    Whether the potential is the density of a functional of a field, moved by its functional derivative.

    		 False
    conserved bool

    Whether the rate is the Laplacian of the derivative of the potential, which conserves the total of a field.

    		 False

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    A state or the divisor is not a name, or the potential is not callable.

    Examples:

...         super().__init__(label, visual=visual)

>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[AmountElement('walker', x=1.0)], interactions=[well])
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=1.0, dt=0.01)
>>> round(float(trajectory.get_values('walker.x')[-1]), 4)

    GroupingInteraction(label, *, target, groups='pairs', act=None, size=2, by=None, capacity=None, phase=None, form='agent', write=None, function=None, reduce='sum')

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that draws groups of members every step and acts on each group.

    At every step of discrete time the interaction splits the members of a group into smaller groups and acts on each of them. The argument groups chooses how they form:

    • 'pairs': disjoint random pairs, and an odd member out forms no group.
    • 'partition': a random partition into groups of size members, the last group holding the rest.
    • 'neighborhood': one group per member, the member first and then the members in the cells or nodes around it.
    • 'state': one group per value of the state by, of at most capacity agents.

    In the agent form the groups act in random order, each through act(members, system) or the method act_on that a subclass overrides. In the symbolic form every member of a group takes the value function(namespace) for the state write at the next step, combined by reduce over the groups that hold it, and a member in no group keeps its value. The namespace of a group holds member, others, the other members in order, members, which the reductions total, mean, count, maximum, and minimum read with over=namespace.members, the time t, and the parameters. The grouping runs in its phase and reads the states that earlier phases of the step set.

    Unlike NeighborInteraction, whose edges are fixed by the space, it draws new groups at every step. Choose it when members meet in random pairs or small groups, such as trades or games, rather than along fixed links.

    It appears in many fields. Agents trade in random pairs, players of a public goods game form groups each round, and animals meet in random encounters that spread information.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'trades'.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ANY,), states=(by, write))]

    The path of the group whose members are grouped.

    		 required
    groups str

    The kind of groups, 'pairs', 'partition', 'neighborhood', or 'state', or in the agent form a PartnerSpec or a function pairing(members, members, rng, capacity) that returns pairs, which group every member with its partners. 'pairs' is a shorthand of PartnerSpec('all', 'uniform', capacity=1).

    		 'pairs'
    act Act | None

    The function of the members of a group and the system view that acts on the group in the agent form, used when a subclass does not override act_on.

    		 None
    size int

    The number of members of a group of a partition.

    		 2
    by str | None

    The name of the state whose values the groups 'state' share.

    		 None
    capacity int | None

    The largest number of agents of a group 'state' in the agent form, or None for no limit.

    		 None
    phase str | None

    The phase of the step the grouping runs in, or None for the default phase.

    		 None
    form str

    'agent' for an action on the agents of every group, or 'symbolic' for a function of every group.

    		 'agent'
    write str | None

    The name of the state that the symbolic form sets.

    		 None
    function GroupFunction | None

    The function of the namespace of one group that returns the value of write for its member, in the symbolic form.

    		 None
    reduce str

    'sum' or 'mean', how the symbolic form combines the values of the groups that hold a member.

    		 'sum'

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    The kind of groups, the form, or the reduction is unknown, the size is below two, the groups 'state' have no state, the capacity is not positive, the symbolic form has no state or function, or a setting of one form is given to the other, raised by prepare.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import GroupingInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> class VoterElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, visual=None, *, s: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
...         super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
...         self.s = s
>>> def adopt_majority(members, system):
...     majority = float(2 * sum(member.s for member in members) > len(members))
...     for member in members:
...         member.s = majority
>>> voters = GroupElement('voters', element=VoterElement, size=3, values={'s': [1.0, 1.0, 0.0]})
>>> galam = GroupingInteraction('galam', target='voters', groups='partition', size=3, act=adopt_majority)
>>> trajectory = simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[voters], interactions=[galam]), until=1)
>>> trajectory.get_agents('voters', 1).values['s'].tolist()
[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]

    In the symbolic form every group of the partition takes the opinion of its majority:

    >>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import mean, where
>>> galam = GroupingInteraction(
...     'galam',
...     target='voters',
...     groups='partition',
...     size=3,
...     form='symbolic',
...     write='s',
...     function=lambda g: where(mean(g.members.s, over=g.members) > 1 / 2, 1, 0),
... )
>>> trajectory = simulate(CompositeSystem(elements=[voters], interactions=[galam]), until=1, random_state=0)
>>> trajectory.get_values('voters.s')[-1].tolist()
[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]

    def act_on(self, members: list[AgentViewProtocol], system: SystemViewProtocol) -> None:
    """Act on the members of one group.

    Args:
        members:
            The agent views of the members of the group.

        system:
            The system view of the rule.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The grouping has neither an action nor its own `act_on`.
    """
    if self.act is None:
        error_msg = f'The grouping {self.label!r} has no action. Pass `act` or override `act_on`.'
        raise ValidationError(error_msg)
    self.act(members, system)

    HamiltonianInteraction(label, *, target, coordinates='q', momenta='p', hamiltonian=None)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that moves canonical pairs by Hamilton's equations.

    A Hamiltonian H is the total energy of a system as a function of its coordinates q and momenta p. The interaction gives Hamilton's equations q' = dH/dp and p' = -dH/dq, one rate per coordinate and per momentum. The coordinates and momenta are states of order 1 of every role that binds one element or group, target by default, and they pair in order. The rates of one state add, so a coupling between two oscillators is an interaction of its own whose Hamiltonian holds only the coupling energy. Dissipation or forcing is a RateInteraction on the momenta.

    Unlike EulerLagrangeInteraction, which takes coordinates and velocities, it takes coordinates and momenta and gives first order rates, which symplectic solvers keep on the surface of constant energy. Choose it when the energy is known in canonical form and long runs must conserve it.

    It appears in many fields. Planets orbit a star, atoms vibrate in a molecule, and charged particles move in a magnetic trap by Hamilton's equations.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'orbit'.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ANY,), states=(coordinates, momenta))]

    The path of the element or group whose states are the canonical pairs.

    		 required
    coordinates str | Sequence[str]

    The name of the state of order 1 that is a coordinate, or the names of several states.

    		 'q'
    momenta str | Sequence[str]

    The name of the state of order 1 that is the momentum of the coordinate, or the names of several states in the order of the coordinates.

    		 'p'
    hamiltonian Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

    A function of the namespace that returns the Hamiltonian.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    A state is not a name, the coordinates and the momenta differ in count, the Hamiltonian is not callable, or a coordinate and its momentum differ in size or are not of order 1.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import HamiltonianInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> class OscillatorElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, q: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0, p: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.q = q
...         self.p = p
>>> energy = lambda s: (s.target.p**2 + s.target.q**2) / 2
>>> spring = HamiltonianInteraction('spring', target='mass', hamiltonian=energy)
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[OscillatorElement('mass')], interactions=[spring])
>>> trajectory = simulate(system, until=3.14159, dt=0.01)
>>> round(float(trajectory.get_values('mass.q')[-1]), 3)

    HyperedgeInteraction(label, size=None)

    Bases: BaseInteraction

    An interaction whose laws run once for every hyperedge of a network.

    A hyperedge is a link that joins more than two nodes, such as a group of three friends. The first role binds a group with one member per node of a network with hyperedges. A second role may bind a group on the hyperedges, or on the edges of one layer. The laws are written for one hyperedge of size members and read:

    • namespace.member, the focal member, whose states rate, noise, and jump laws change,
    • namespace.others, the other members in the order of the hyperedge, a tuple of namespaces,
    • namespace.members, all the members, which total, mean, count, maximum, and minimum reduce with over=namespace.members,
    • namespace.hyperedge, the member of the group on hyperedges,
    • namespace.edge, the member of the group on edges that joins the first two members,
    • the parameters of the interaction.

    A law of the focal member runs once per member of every hyperedge. A law that targets the member on a hyperedge or an edge runs once per hyperedge, with the first member as the focal member.

    Unlike NeighborInteraction, which sees the two ends of an edge, it sees every member of a group link at once. Choose it when a change depends on a whole group, such as a majority of three, and not on pairs alone.

    It appears in many fields. Group conversations shift opinions, a disease spreads within households and classrooms, and three species compete at once in higher-order ecological models.

    JumpInteraction(label, *, target, changes=None, rate=None, probability=None, waiting=None, reset=None)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction whose random events change states by signed amounts.

    When the event fires it adds changes to the states of the target, such as minus one infected and plus one recovered. Exactly one clock says when it fires:

    • rate: at the times of a Poisson process of that propensity, in continuous time.
    • probability: with that probability in a step of discrete time.
    • waiting: after a time drawn anew at every firing, as in a renewal process. Each member of a group then fires on its own clock, and reset sets states to new values at each firing.

    Every function reads namespace.target, the states and parameters of the target, and the time namespace.t.

    Unlike RateInteraction, which changes a state continuously, it changes states by whole amounts at random times. Choose it when the units are few enough that their randomness matters, as in the stochastic simulation algorithm of Gillespie.

    It appears in many fields. Births and deaths change a population one at a time, customers join and leave a queue, molecules react in a small cell volume, and a machine fails and is repaired.

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'births'.

    LocalRuleInteraction(label, *, target, state, rule, neighborhood, reads=None, schedule='synchronous', stochastic=False)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that sets the next value of each cell from its neighbourhood.

    A cellular automaton is a lattice or network of cells whose values change by one local rule at every step. The rule maps the ordered values of the neighbourhood of a cell to its next value. It takes one of these forms:

    • TableSpec: a table of the next value for every configuration of the neighbourhood.
    • TotalisticSpec: a rule of the sum of the neighbourhood.
    • OuterTotalisticSpec: a rule of the cell and the sum of its neighbours, as in the Game of Life.
    • An object whose get_table() returns a TableSpec.
    • A function that receives one array per neighbour of every read state, in neighbourhood order, and returns the next values, one array per state. With stochastic it also receives a uniform random array random, and it receives the parameters of the group by name.

    A state of several components per cell reaches a function as one row of components per cell. A StateTranslationNeighborhood reads a group space at the product of each site and the group element that the first read state holds there.

    Unlike MapInteraction, which writes the next value as an expression of one member, it reads an ordered neighbourhood and may take a table. Choose it when the next value of a cell depends on the exact pattern around it.

    It appears in many fields. Conway's Game of Life, the sandpile of Bak, Tang, and Wiesenfeld, forest fire models, and models of traffic on a ring road are cellular automata.

    MapInteraction(label, *, target, state, function, sources=(), mode='replace', schedule='synchronous', form='symbolic', phase=None)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that sets the next value of a state at every discrete step.

    With mode='replace' the next value of the state is f, and with mode='increment' it is the state plus f. The schedule says in what order the members of a group update:

    • 'synchronous': all at once, from the states at the start of the step.
    • 'sequential': one after another in their order, each reading the values set before it.
    • 'random-sequential': one after another in a new random order every step.
    • 'member': in the agent form, each member in its own activation, with the rules of its element.

    In the symbolic form function(namespace) returns an expression, or a vector of them for a vector state. namespace.target holds the states and parameters of the target, namespace.sources the namespaces of the sources, and namespace.t the time, and the expression may hold draws such as normal('noise'). In the agent form the target is an agent group and function(agent, system) returns a number or an array, so it can read the agent, its neighbours, and the history and storage of the system.

    Unlike RateInteraction, which gives a derivative in continuous time, it gives the next value in discrete time. Choose it when the model steps, such as a yearly census or a round of a game.

    It appears in many fields. The logistic map follows a population from year to year, an account compounds interest once a month, and agents update their wealth after each round of an exchange.

    NeighborInteraction(label, layer=None)

    Bases: BaseInteraction

    An interaction whose laws run once for every edge of a network or lattice.

    A role binds a group with one member per node or site, and a second role may bind a group on the edges of the same network, such as the conductance of each line of a power grid. The laws are written for one edge. They read namespace.source and namespace.target, the members at its two ends, namespace.edge, the member of the edge group, and the parameters. On a directed graph the ends follow the direction of the edge, and on an undirected graph the source comes first in node order. On fixed edges namespace.source.degree and namespace.target.degree are the numbers of edges at each end.

    A law that reads no edge member and only one end outside its reductions runs once per member, not once per edge. Inside a reduction the other end stands for the other members, so mean(f(s.source.x, s.target.x), over=s.source) is the mean of f over the neighbours of each target. A second role may also bind a second group of nodes, with no edges, and the reductions then run over its members. Roles may bind separate elements too, and namespace.source is then the tuple of their namespaces. A subclass that names its ends otherwise returns their names from _get_role.

    Unlike Interaction, which runs once per bound member, it runs once per edge, so each law sees both ends of a link. Choose it when a change flows along the links of a lattice or network, such as diffusion or a flow on a line.

    It appears in many fields. Heat flows between neighbouring cells of a lattice, a disease spreads along the contacts of a network, and power flows along the lines of a grid.

    label str

    PairInteraction(label, first, second, cutoff=1.0, position='x', *, write='x', function=None, potential=None, divisor=None, period=None)

    Bases: BaseInteraction

    An interaction whose laws run for every pair of members within a cutoff.

    The pairs are those whose vector states position lie closer than cutoff. The laws are written for one pair and read namespace.first, the member that receives the value, namespace.second, the other member, and the parameters. Each member adds a value to the rate of its state write, which is the highest derivative of a state of any order:

    • With function, the value is function(namespace), or one value per state when write names several.
    • With potential, a function potential(namespace, r) of the distance r, the value is minus the gradient of the potential with respect to the member's own position.

    A divisor divides the value, such as a mass. With neither a function nor a potential, a subclass writes its own laws in _get_laws, and a subclass that names the members otherwise returns their names from _get_role.

    Unlike NeighborInteraction, whose links are fixed edges, it finds its pairs by distance at every evaluation. Choose it when members move in continuous space and act on those close by.

    It appears in many fields. Atoms of a gas repel under the Lennard-Jones potential, stars attract by gravity within a cutoff, and pedestrians keep their distance in a crowd.

    RateInteraction(label, *, target, state='x', rate=0.0, sources=(), noise=None, divisor=None, process=None, index=None, convention='ito', hurst=None, conserved=False)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that adds a rate and a noise to the derivative of a state.

    The rate rate(namespace) and the noise noise(namespace) dW add to the highest time derivative of the state. On a state of order 1 the rate is its first derivative, and on a state of order k it adds to the kth derivative, so rates on one state add up. A divisor d, such as an inertia or a capacitance, divides the rate and the noise.

    A rate, noise, or divisor function takes a namespace with the target as target, the elements it reads as sources, the time t, and the parameters a subclass declares. A number stands for a constant, and a number on a vector state applies to every component. The noise is an independent Wiener process per component and member by default, the random walk of continuous time.

    Unlike MapInteraction, which steps a state in discrete time, it gives the derivative of a state in continuous time, with an optional noise. Choose it when a state flows, as in an ordinary or a stochastic differential equation.

    It appears in many fields. Infected people recover at a rate, a balance grows by interest, a capacitor charges through a resistor, and a stock price follows a geometric Brownian motion.

    		 None

    		 None

    		 None

    The process of process that drives the noise, or None for every process, one per component of a vector state.

    SamplingInteraction(label, *, target, state, objective, move='flip', intensity=1.0, rule='metropolis', schedule='checkerboard', neighborhood=None, values=(), width=1.0, cooling=None)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that samples a state of the members by Monte Carlo moves.

    In each unit of time the interaction makes one sweep. A sweep proposes a new value of the state of every member and accepts it by the change of the local objective of the member, the terms of the objective that involve its value, scaled by intensity. The objective is a function of the namespace, which holds namespace.target, the member, and namespace.target.other, a neighbour, whose values neighbors(...) sums over neighborhood. The argument move proposes the new values:

    • 'flip': the negative of the value, as for a spin of plus or minus one.
    • 'random-value': a value drawn from values.
    • 'rotate': the value plus a uniform number in [-width, width].
    • 'gaussian': the value plus a normal number of standard deviation width.
    • 'cluster': the Wolff algorithm, which flips whole clusters of aligned neighbours at once.
    • A function move(values, random) that returns the proposed values.

    A group on the edges of a cell complex takes an objective that sums over CofaceNeighborhood, and its 'colored' schedule updates together only links that share no face.

    Unlike MapInteraction, which sets the next value by a rule, it proposes values and accepts them by a probability, so the states follow a stationary distribution. Choose it when the model is a Boltzmann distribution of an energy, as in a Markov chain Monte Carlo method.

    It appears in many fields. Spins of a magnet in the Ising model, cells of a tissue in the cellular Potts model, and residents who move in a model of segregation are sampled this way.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'spins'.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec(elements=(ANY,), states=(state,))]

    The path of the group on the sites of a lattice, the nodes of a network, or the edges of a cell complex.

    		 required
    state str

    The name of the state the moves change.

    		 required
    objective Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | BaseSpec

    The function objective(namespace) of the local objective of a member, or the score spec of a subclass that samples by its own law.

    		 required
    move str | Callable[..., object]

    How a new value is proposed, one of the moves above. The move 'cluster' grows each cluster from a random member through the bonds to its neighbours with the probability 1 - exp(min(0, -intensity * (f(-s, n) - f(s, n)))), where f(s, n) is the term of the objective for a member of value s and a neighbour of value n. A sweep flips clusters until as many members have flipped as there are members. It needs an objective of such pair terms that flipping both values keeps, and it ignores rule and schedule.

    		 'flip'
    intensity Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=POSITIVE_VALUES)]

    The factor of the change of the objective in the acceptance exp(-intensity * change), positive and possibly infinite.

    		 1.0
    rule str

    The acceptance, 'metropolis', 'glauber', or 'heat-bath', which draws among all values of a discrete move by the weights exp(-intensity * objective).

    		 'metropolis'
    schedule str

    'checkerboard', 'colored', or 'random-sequential'.

    		 'checkerboard'
    neighborhood BaseNeighborhood | None

    The neighbourhood the objective reduces over, or None for the von Neumann neighbourhood of a square lattice. A network takes AdjacencyNeighborhood().

    		 None
    values Sequence[float]

    The values a random-value move draws from.

    		 ()
    width float

    The largest change of a rotation, or the standard deviation of a Gaussian move.

    		 1.0
    cooling Callable[[Expression], object] | None

    The function of the time symbol that multiplies one over the intensity, or None for a constant intensity.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    The move, the rule, or the schedule is unknown, or the objective is not callable, raised by prepare.

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import SamplingInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import neighbors
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import DiscreteTime, LatticeSpace
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> class SpinElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, s: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.s = s
>>> objective = lambda n: -n.target.s * neighbors(n.target.other.s)
>>> ising = SamplingInteraction('ising', target='spins', state='s', objective=objective, intensity=1.0)
>>> spins = GroupElement('spins', element=SpinElement, space=LatticeSpace((8, 8)), on='sites')
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[spins], interactions=[ising], time=DiscreteTime())
>>> states = simulate(system, until=20, random_state=0).states
>>> bool(abs(states[-1].mean()) > 0.9)
True
>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import cos
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import exterior_derivative
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import CellComplexSpace, CofaceNeighborhood
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> class LinkElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, theta: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.theta = theta
>>> wilson = lambda n: -neighbors(cos(exterior_derivative(n.target.theta)), over=CofaceNeighborhood())
>>> gauge = SamplingInteraction(
...     'wilson', target='links', state='theta', objective=wilson, move='rotate', schedule='colored'
... )
>>> links = GroupElement('links', element=LinkElement, space=CellComplexSpace(LatticeSpace((4, 4))), on='edges')
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[links], interactions=[gauge], time=DiscreteTime())
>>> simulate(system, until=2, random_state=0).states.shape
(3, 32)

    TopologyInteraction(label, *, target=None, action='add-edge', rate=None, probability=None, condition=None, toward=None, edges=1, keep='source', values=None, layer=None, hyperedge=None, independent=False, direction='out', candidates=1, score=None, one=False, inherit=1.0, parent=0.0)

    Bases: NeighborInteraction

    An interaction that adds, removes, and rewires the nodes and edges of a network.

    The action runs for every node of the group the target binds, or for every edge of its network, and fires at a rate, with a probability per step, or always, where condition holds. The groups on the nodes and edges of the network are variable. The actions are:

    • 'add-node': a new node joins edges other nodes. Without a target it adds one node from outside per step, as in a growing network.
    • 'remove-node' and 'replace-node': the node leaves, or leaves and a new node takes its place in one request.
    • 'add-edge': the node joins edges other nodes, or with candidates the candidate of the smallest score.
    • 'remove-edge' and 'rewire': the edge leaves, or keeps its end keep and moves its other end.
    • 'add-hyperedge' and 'remove-hyperedge': a node forms a hyperedge of size hyperedge, or a hyperedge leaves.
    • 'close-triangle': the node joins two of its neighbours that are not yet joined.
    • 'contract-edge': a neighbour merges into the node, which keeps the union of their links.
    • 'duplicate-node': a copy of the node inherits each of its links with probability inherit.

    The rate, the probability, and the condition are numbers or functions of the namespace of an edge, whose ends are namespace.source and namespace.target, and an action on a node reads the node as the source. New ends are drawn with probability proportional to toward, or uniformly. A new node or edge takes values.

    Unlike NeighborInteraction, which runs on fixed edges, it changes the edges and nodes themselves during a run. Choose it when the network grows, shrinks, or rewires as the system runs, so structure and states change together.

    It appears in many fields. Preferential attachment grows the web and citation networks, people rewire their contacts to avoid infection, genes duplicate in the evolution of protein networks, and friends of friends close triangles in social networks.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'attachment'.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec(optional=True, elements=(ANY,))]

    The path of the group on the nodes of the network, of the variable group on its hyperedges for 'remove-hyperedge', or None for an addition of one node or of edges between drawn nodes per step.

    		 None
    action str

    The change, 'add-node', 'remove-node', 'replace-node', 'add-edge', 'remove-edge', 'rewire', 'add-hyperedge', 'remove-hyperedge', 'close-triangle', 'contract-edge', or 'duplicate-node'.

    		 'add-edge'
    rate Chance | None

    The rate of the change, a number or a function, or None for a probability per step.

    		 None
    probability Chance | None

    The probability of the change per step, a number or a function, or None for probability one.

    		 None
    condition Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

    A function of the namespace that returns where the change may fire, or None everywhere.

    		 None
    toward Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

    A function of the namespace of a candidate node that returns its weight as a new end, reading the node the new edge starts from as namespace.source, or None for equal weights.

    		 None
    edges int

    The number of edges a new node or a node adding edges joins.

    		 1
    keep str

    The end of an edge a rewiring keeps, 'source' or 'target'.

    		 'source'
    values Mapping[str, object] | None

    		 None
    layer str | None

    The layer of the network whose edges change, or None for the graph of the network.

    		 None
    hyperedge int | None

    The size of the hyperedge every new node or every node of 'add-hyperedge' forms with existing nodes, or None for none.

    		 None
    independent bool

    Whether every candidate becomes a new end on its own with the probability toward, in place of edges ends drawn by weight.

    		 False
    direction str

    The direction of new edges on a directed layer, 'out' of the node, 'in' to it, or 'both'.

    TrainingInteraction(label, *, system, trained, loss, data, optimizer='adam', learning_rate=0.001, momentum=0.9, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, batch_size=32, truncation=None, metrics=())

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that trains the parameters of a nested system by gradient steps.

    The role system binds a nested system, which the training runs over the sequences of a dataset from its initial states and differentiates. One step of the outer system is one epoch: shuffled batches, each followed by one update of the optimizer on the adaptive parameters named in trained. The hyperparameters of the optimizer are parameters of the interaction, so a schedule of simulate can change them between epochs. The optimizer reads them as follows:

    • 'sgd': the learning rate.
    • 'momentum': the learning rate and momentum.
    • 'rmsprop': the learning rate and beta2, the decay of its mean squared gradient.
    • 'adam': the learning rate, beta1, and beta2.

    Unlike GradientInteraction, which moves states down a potential in the time of the system, it fits parameters of another system to data, one epoch per step. Choose it when a part of the model learns from data during the run.

    It appears in many fields. A recurrent neural network learns to predict a time series, an echo state network fits its readout, and a learning agent improves its policy between rounds.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'training'.

    The path of the nested system whose parameters the interaction trains.

    		 required
    trained Sequence[str]

    The dotted paths of the adaptive parameters of the nested system to train, such as readout.W.

    		 required
    loss ObservableSpec

    The observable of the nested system whose weighted mean over the steps of a batch is minimized.

    		 required
    data DatasetSpec

    The sequences of the parameters of the nested system that set its inputs and targets at every step.

    		 required
    optimizer str

    The name of the optimizer, one of OPTIMIZERS.

    		 'adam'
    learning_rate Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The learning rate of the optimizer.

    		 0.001
    momentum Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, 1))]

    The momentum of 'momentum'.

    		 0.9
    beta1 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, 1))]

    The decay of the mean gradient of 'adam'.

    		 0.9
    beta2 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, 1))]

    The decay of the mean squared gradient of 'adam' and 'rmsprop'.

    		 0.999
    batch_size int

    The number of sequences of a batch.

    		 32
    truncation int | None

    The number of inner steps the gradient flows back through the inner states, or None for the whole run. A truncation of 1 holds the previous inner states as constant inputs, as Elman's original training does.

    		 None
    metrics Sequence[ObservableSpec]

    The observables of the nested system recorded at the end of every epoch.

>>> training = TrainingInteraction(
...     'training', system='net', trained=['readout.W'], loss=ObservableSpec('error', 0.0), data=data
... )

    TransferInteraction(label, *, source, target, state, into=None, amount, flow='', pairing='members', legs=(), fallback=None, guard=None, rate=None, reverse_rate=None, offset=0, boundary='periodic', form='symbolic', schedule='random-sequential', actor='source', partners=None, remove=None, phase=None, settlement=None)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that moves amounts of states from one member to another.

    A leg moves an amount out of a state of the source member, or out of Source(), the environment, into a state of the target member, or into Sink(). The first leg moves amount from state into into, and legs add more. All amounts are read before any moves, so each leg sees the states as they were before the transfer. What a source state loses, the target state gains, unless a leg starts at Source() or ends at Sink(). A guard skips the transfer where it does not hold.

    The argument form chooses how the transfer runs:

    • 'symbolic': transfer laws between the source and the target of one element, or between member i of both groups. The amounts, the guard, and the rates are numbers or functions of the namespace, which reads the roles as namespace.source and namespace.target. With a rate the amount moves in jumps, and with offset each member transfers to the member offset places along the group. Every leg is reported as a flow.
    • 'agent': an agent rule, whose amounts and guard are functions of the source agent, the target agent, and the system view. The members are paired by pairing, and the pairs act in random order, or each member of actor acts in its own activation under the schedule 'member'.

    A leg end '<role>.<state>' names a state of the element another role binds, so one transfer moves amounts between several holders, such as the payments of a circuit of sectors. A leg end of the agent form may also name '<reference>.<state>', the state of the member that a reference state of the agent names, such as 'bank.deposits' for the deposits of a customer's bank. A subclass that names its roles otherwise returns their names from _get_role.

    Unlike RateInteraction, which changes one state, it takes from one state what it adds to another, so the amount is conserved. Choose it when a quantity moves between holders, such as money, people, or mass.

    It appears in many fields. People move from susceptible to infected in an epidemic, money flows between accounts in an economy, water flows between reservoirs, and predators gain the biomass of the prey they eat.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The name of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system, such as 'infection'.

    		 required

    		 required

A named flow is reported as <path>.<flow> when the source and the target are one element or group, and as <label>.<flow> otherwise. A leg without a name is reported as <label>.flow_<index>.

    		 ''
    pairing str | Pairing | PartnerSpec

    How members are paired. The symbolic form takes 'members' alone.

    • 'members': member i of the source with member i of the target.
    • 'random': every source member with a random target member.
    • 'pairs': disjoint random pairs.
    • 'neighbors': every source member with the target members in the cells or nodes around it.
    • 'neighbor-pairs': disjoint random pairs of neighbours.
    • 'cell': the source and target members that stand in one cell or node.
    • 'site': every source member with the site of a target field at its cell, where a negative amount takes from the site and the functions take the cell in place of a target agent.

    The agent form also takes a PartnerSpec, which pairs members within a radius, by score, or with a fallback, or a function pairing(sources, targets, rng, capacity) that returns pairs, whose capacity is partners, or 1 without it. Under the schedule 'member' it receives the actor alone as its first sequence, and the partners of the actor are the second items of its pairs.

    def transfer(self, source: AgentViewProtocol, target: AgentViewProtocol, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> bool:
    """Move the amounts of every leg from one source agent to one target agent.

    It moves them when the guard holds.

    Args:
        source:
            The agent the amounts leave.

        target:
            The agent the amounts enter.

        system:
            The system view of the rule.

    Returns:
        transferred:
            Whether the guard held, so the amounts moved.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            An amount function returns something other than a number.

        SimulationError:
            A leg end names the state of a referenced member, and the reference state names no member.
    """
    if self.guard is not None and not self.guard(source, target, system):
        return False
    legs = self._get_legs()
    amounts = [self._evaluate(amount, source, target, system) for _, _, amount, _ in legs]
    if self.settlement is not None:
        self.settlement(source, target, amounts, system)
        return True
    ends = [
        (
            self._get_end(source, state) if isinstance(state, str) else None,
            self._get_end(target, into) if isinstance(into, str) else None,
        )
        for state, into, _, _ in legs
    ]
    for (taken, given), amount in zip(ends, amounts, strict=True):
        if taken is not None:
            holder, name = taken
            setattr(holder, name, getattr(holder, name) - amount)
        if given is not None:
            holder, name = given
            setattr(holder, name, getattr(holder, name) + amount)
    return True

    TransitionInteraction(label, *, target, state='state', source=0.0, destination=1.0, rate=None, probability=None, condition=None, matrix=None, emission=None, observed=None, over='member', neighborhood=None, after=None, schedule='synchronous', form='symbolic', phase=None)

    Bases: Interaction

    An interaction that moves a discrete state from one value to another.

    A member whose state holds source moves to destination, by exactly one of these kinds:

    • rate: as a jump in continuous time.
    • probability: with that probability in each step of discrete time.
    • condition: in the step in which the condition holds.
    • matrix: by the row of a transition matrix for the current value, in discrete time, as a Markov chain. An emission matrix then draws the observed state from the row of the next value, as a hidden Markov model.

    With over='neighbors' the rate and the probability are those of one neighbour, read as namespace.target.other. The rates of the neighbours add up, and their probabilities combine as 1 - prod(1 - p). With after, a member moves only once it has held the source value for that many steps. In the symbolic form every function reads namespace.target and the time namespace.t. In the agent form every function takes the agent and the system view, f(agent, system), and a rate r moves an agent with probability 1 - exp(-r) in a step. With over='cell' each member acts on the other members of its cell, by f(agent, other, system).

    Unlike JumpInteraction, which adds amounts to numeric states, it moves a categorical state between named values. Choose it when each member is in one of a few states, such as healthy, sick, and immune.

    It appears in many fields. A person moves from susceptible to infected in an epidemic on a network, a voter switches opinion, a cell of a forest catches fire, and a customer switches between brands.

    def move(self, system: SystemViewProtocol) -> None:
    """Move the state of every agent of the target that moves in this step.

    The agents follow the schedule.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the interaction.
    """
    agents = list(system.get_agents(self._get_role('target')))
    if self.schedule == 'synchronous':
        moves = [move for agent in agents for move in self._get_moves(agent, system)]
        self._apply(moves, system)
        return
    order = system.rng.permutation(len(agents)) if self.schedule == 'random-sequential' else range(len(agents))
    for index in order:
        self._move_member(agents[int(index)], system)
